paragraphs: This paper asks whether the changing visual experiences of infants can help explain how visual learning develops. As infants become more mobile, what they see becomes more varied and dynamic. The researchers used videos recorded by infant head-mounted cameras to investigate whether the order of those experiences matters when training artificial visual learning systems.

They divided the recordings by age and trained several self-supervised models with curricula that reflected developmental order. Starting with footage from the youngest infants produced the strongest learning signal and the best performance on subsequent tasks. The study further attributes the usefulness of this early footage to its slower changes and simpler visual content.

The findings suggest that training data matter through their progression as well as their contents. Relatively simple, slowly changing experiences can provide a useful starting point before more complex inputs arrive. These are empirical results from artificial learning models, supporting the importance of early experience without establishing that the models reproduce the learning mechanisms of infant brains.
neurips-2023-curriculum-learning-with-in.tldr: Models trained first on the youngest infants’ slower, simpler visual experiences achieved the best downstream learning outcomes.

paragraphs: D4 examines whether language models can learn more efficiently by choosing training documents carefully. A common approach trains once on a large, randomly selected collection of web text. Although adding more data generally improves performance, the improvements shrink with scale, motivating a closer look at which documents deserve the available training compute.

The method uses representations from a pretrained model to select data after duplicate removal. This makes document selection an additional step beyond simply eliminating repeated text. At the 6.7-billion-parameter scale, the authors report 20% training efficiency gains and improvements of up to 2% in average downstream accuracy across 16 language tasks.

The paper also tests repetition and finds that intelligently repeating selected data consistently beats baseline training, whereas repeating random data performs worse. That distinction makes the result more specific than a recommendation to reuse data indiscriminately. The evidence challenges the assumption that one pass through as much randomly sampled text as possible is always the best use of a training budget.
neurips-2023-d4-improving-llm-pretrainin.tldr: Careful document selection and intelligent repetition improved language-model training efficiency and downstream accuracy beyond duplicate removal alone.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to discover previously unseen categories of 3D objects in unlabeled data using knowledge learned from different, labeled categories. Features trained to recognize known categories can be too closely tied to those categories. The authors instead focus on geometric parts, which can recur across objects belonging to otherwise different classes.

Their method, DNIK, learns a bank of part concepts from known classes and represents unfamiliar shapes as combinations of those concepts. Three constraints encourage the bank to contain diverse concepts rather than collapse into repetitive representations. A separate part relation module incorporates spatial relationships, allowing recognition to use both the parts present and how those parts are arranged.

The authors construct three evaluation tasks and report average improvements of 11.7%, 14.1%, and 16.3% over state-of-the-art baselines on those tasks. These findings support parts as a useful basis for transferring knowledge across categories. The central contribution is a representation that makes unfamiliar whole objects describable through reusable geometric components.
neurips-2023-decompose-novel-into-known-.tldr: DNIK discovers unfamiliar 3D object categories by representing shapes through reusable part concepts and their spatial relationships.

paragraphs: DISCO-10M addresses a practical obstacle in machine learning for music: datasets can be too small, difficult to access, or lacking in audio resources. The paper introduces a music dataset that the authors describe as an order of magnitude larger than the largest previously available collection. Its contribution centers on providing a broader resource for research.

The authors pair this scale with a multistage filtering process intended to improve data quality. Filtering incorporates similarity information from both textual descriptions and audio embeddings. Using these two kinds of information lets the curation process draw on descriptions of the music as well as representations of its audio content.

The release also includes precomputed CLAP embeddings, giving researchers representations they can use directly in downstream tasks. This reduces the preparation needed to begin exploring applications on the dataset. The stated goal is to make music research more accessible and support new models; the abstract presents dataset scale, filtering, and ready-to-use representations as the means toward that goal.
neurips-2023-disco-10m-a-large-scale-mus.tldr: DISCO-10M provides a substantially larger music dataset with multistage filtering and precomputed embeddings for downstream research.

paragraphs: This paper proposes a way to check whether a model was trained on a protected dataset. The authors identify a problem with backdoor-based ownership verification: adversaries can exploit the introduced behavior to cause malicious misclassification. Their alternative makes the identifying behavior successful classification of difficult examples, rather than an intentionally incorrect response.

The method constructs a domain of examples that a model trained on the original dataset struggles to classify correctly. Modified training samples make this domain easier for a model trained on the protected dataset. A two-level optimization produces visually indistinguishable modifications while retaining the samples’ correct labels, aiming to create the identifying effect without an obvious watermark.

Ownership verification then uses a hypothesis test based on performance in the watermark domain. The paper supplies theoretical analysis and experiments on three benchmark datasets, reporting effective verification and resistance to the adaptive methods evaluated. The contribution is a behavioral signature tied to learning difficult examples correctly, with empirical support for both its detectability and its concealment.
neurips-2023-domain-watermark-effective-.tldr: Domain Watermark verifies dataset use through correct predictions on specially constructed difficult examples instead of backdoor-induced misclassification.

paragraphs: Regression models often need to predict both an outcome and how uncertain that prediction is. This paper distinguishes uncertainty inherent in observations from uncertainty about the model itself. It focuses on heteroscedastic regression, where the amount of observation noise changes with the input rather than remaining constant across all examples.

Training a Gaussian predictor directly through its mean and variance can compromise the mean prediction because predictive variance scales the training gradients. The authors instead use the Gaussian’s natural parameterization, drawing on its established stability in related settings. They also emphasize regularization of both network parameters and predictions, rather than treating the parameterization change as the entire solution.

An efficient Laplace approximation supplies model uncertainty and enables automatic regularization through empirical Bayes. Across regression problems, including a new image regression benchmark with varying noise, the authors report scalability and improvements over previous approaches. Their method provides epistemic uncertainty without requiring hyperparameter tuning, connecting uncertainty estimation with a practical mechanism for improving generalization.
neurips-2023-effective-bayesian-heterosc.tldr: A different Gaussian parameterization and efficient Bayesian approximation improve regression with input-dependent noise and model uncertainty.

paragraphs: Neural populations vary in their responses even when experimental conditions repeat. The covariance of those fluctuations describes how neurons vary together and influences the population’s ability to carry signals. Estimating it separately for every condition can require many repeated trials, making rich experiments with few repetitions difficult to analyze.

The authors use Wishart process models to share statistical information across nearby conditions. Their approach exploits experiments in which conditions have a smooth parameterization, so neighboring settings can inform one another. Instead of obtaining isolated covariance estimates, the model produces a smoothly varying description of covariance across stimulus parameters.

On recordings from mouse visual cortex and monkey motor cortex, the models compare favorably with standard covariance estimators. They also support predictions of noise correlations at unobserved conditions and continuous estimates of Fisher information, a measure of signal fidelity. These results suggest a useful route to estimating neural variability and its uncertainty when trials are scarce, provided the structure across conditions can be exploited.
neurips-2023-estimating-noise-correlatio.tldr: Wishart process models estimate neural noise correlations with few trials by sharing information across smoothly varying experimental conditions.

paragraphs: This paper studies fairness when indivisible chores must be distributed among people whose costs for bundles need not equal the sum of individual task costs. It uses maximin share fairness as the benchmark. Because exact fairness cannot always be achieved, the question is how closely an allocation can approximate that benchmark under different cost structures.

For submodular costs, the authors prove that no algorithm can guarantee an approximation better than the smaller of n and log(m)/log(log(m)), where n counts agents and m counts tasks. For subadditive costs, they establish existence of an allocation with factor min(n, ceil(log(m))). They also show that the ordinal relaxation called 1-out-of-d MMS can fail to exist for any d of at least two.

The picture improves for two structured applications: bin packing and job scheduling. Both admit constant approximations under multiplicative and ordinal fairness relaxations. The results therefore distinguish broad nonadditive cost classes, where strong fairness guarantees face serious barriers, from specific task structures where useful guarantees remain possible.
neurips-2023-fair-allocation-of-indivisi.tldr: Strong fairness guarantees face barriers for general nonadditive chores, while bin packing and job scheduling admit constant approximations.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether a pretrained image classifier can provide enough information to train an image generator without any data samples. A classifier extracts information useful for recognition, so reconstructing a generator from its outputs alone appears difficult. The authors instead use knowledge contained in the classifier’s network parameters as the source of training information.

Their approach draws on the maximum-margin bias of gradient descent. Rather than supplying real images as examples for the generator, they train it so that its generated sample distribution satisfies convergence conditions associated with the classifier’s parameters. This turns properties of how the classifier learned into constraints on the distribution the generator should produce.

Experiments on several image generation tasks support the effectiveness of this strategy. The result suggests that trained classifier parameters can contain useful generative information beyond the predictions they directly produce. The contribution is a learning framework for extracting that information without data samples, supported by empirical validation rather than a claim that every classifier uniquely determines its original training distribution.
neurips-2023-generator-born-from-classif.tldr: A generator learns without data samples by making generated distributions satisfy learning-related conditions encoded in a pretrained classifier’s parameters.

paragraphs: People can learn many structured patterns from relatively little evidence. This paper investigates whether that combination of flexibility and data efficiency can be explained by learning probabilistic programs. In this account, a learner considers structured rules that could have generated the observations and updates beliefs about those rules as more evidence arrives.

Participants repeatedly predicted where a dot would move in two dimensions based on its earlier trajectory. The researchers compared human behavior with standard parametric and nonparametric time-series models. They also tested two Bayesian program synthesis models: a compositional Gaussian process model and a more structured Language of Thought model, providing hypotheses with different kinds of organization.

The Language of Thought model best explained the observed signatures of human pattern learning. This supports the idea that inference over an expressive collection of programs can account for flexible learning from small amounts of data. The evidence concerns behavior in the tested spatial and temporal prediction task, offering a computational explanation rather than establishing that people literally execute the model’s algorithm.
neurips-2023-human-spatiotemporal-patter.tldr: Human dot-trajectory predictions were best explained by Bayesian inference over a structured Language of Thought program space.

paragraphs: Federated bandit learning lets multiple clients contribute information to a shared learning process while making decisions over time. Many existing methods assume clients willingly share data whenever the server needs it. This paper instead considers self-interested clients who may decline to communicate unless doing so provides an explicit benefit.

The authors formulate an incentivized communication problem in which the server must motivate clients to share information. They instantiate it for contextual linear bandits and introduce Inc-FedUCB. Its design treats learning performance, communication, and incentive expenditure as connected requirements, so obtaining useful data includes accounting for the willingness of clients to provide it.

The protocol achieves near-optimal regret together with provable guarantees on communication and incentive costs. Experiments using synthetic and real-world datasets further support its effectiveness across the evaluated environments. The paper’s main significance is bringing participation incentives into the learning formulation: a communication-efficient algorithm also needs a reason for self-interested clients to follow its communication requests.
neurips-2023-incentivized-communication-.tldr: Inc-FedUCB incentivizes self-interested clients to share bandit data while providing regret, communication, and incentive-cost guarantees.

paragraphs: A learning algorithm can satisfy a regret guarantee without maximizing the reward available against another learner. This paper studies that tension in repeated two-player games. It introduces generalized equilibria that allow the players to have different regret constraints and characterize their feasible rewards. Those equilibria are reachable by algorithms that retain their regret guarantees against arbitrary opponents.

A central case pairs a player with no swap regret against one without a regret constraint. This extends Stackelberg equilibria with a matching optimal value. In a broad class of games, including almost every game without a pure Nash equilibrium, a player can gain substantially by departing from no-swap-regret behavior when facing a no-swap learner.

Learning a reward-optimal strategy in an initially unknown game also depends on the opponent’s algorithm. For games where the Stackelberg strategy is learnable through queries, the paper gives exponential-time learning against any no-regret agent and polynomial-time learning against any no-adaptive-regret agent. Additional separations show that regret guarantees alone do not determine how readily an opponent can be learned against.
neurips-2023-is-learning-in-games-good-f.tldr: Regret guarantees can trade off with achievable reward, and an opponent’s learning algorithm affects both optimal play and its learnability.

paragraphs: LEPARD reconstructs an animal’s articulated 3D shape from a single image taken in an uncontrolled setting. It approaches the animal as a collection of meaningful parts. This decomposition is useful because individual parts usually have simpler shapes than the entire animal and remain useful units of representation as articulation changes the overall pose.

The framework represents parts explicitly as parameterized primitive surfaces in three dimensions. Global and local deformations adjust these surfaces to match evidence in the image. An optimization procedure inspired by kinematics guides the transformations using two-dimensional evidence, connecting the reconstruction process to the movement and arrangement of the component parts.

Training uses existing DINO deep features and requires no 2D or 3D annotations. In animal reconstruction experiments, the authors report significant improvements over existing alternatives in both overall reconstruction and discovery of consistent, semantically meaningful parts. The findings support explicit part representations as a way to address shape and articulation together while avoiding the need for manually annotated training targets.
neurips-2023-lepard-learning-explicit-pa.tldr: LEPARD reconstructs articulated 3D animals through explicit deformable parts, learning from DINO features without 2D or 3D annotations.

paragraphs: Sequence memory requires a system to store patterns together with the order in which they should be recalled. Recurrent Hopfield-like networks can learn such sequences through temporally asymmetric learning rules, but interference between memories limits the sequence length they can hold. This paper changes the interactions within these networks to reduce that interference.

Inspired by dense associative memories, the authors introduce a nonlinear interaction term that increases separation between patterns. They derive new laws describing how maximum sequence length scales with network size and verify them numerically. These laws improve substantially on the existing scaling results for models based on traditional Hopfield networks.

The paper also introduces a generalized pseudoinverse learning rule for recalling sequences whose patterns are highly correlated. A further extension allows different amounts of time between successive states, expanding the model beyond a fixed transition rhythm. Together with a proposed biologically plausible implementation and connections to motor neuroscience, these contributions address sequence length, pattern similarity, and timing as distinct requirements of sequence memory.
neurips-2023-long-sequence-hopfield-memo.tldr: Nonlinear interactions expand Hopfield-like sequence capacity, with additional mechanisms for correlated patterns and variable transition timing.

paragraphs: Procedural content generation can automatically produce game environments, but producing content that reflects a particular intention remains challenging. MarioGPT explores whether a language model can make generation more controllable through text. It uses a fine-tuned GPT2 model to create tile-based Super Mario Bros levels, applying an existing language model to a new kind of structured output.

Text prompts guide the kinds of levels the model generates. This addresses the gap between obtaining varied content and obtaining content shaped by a user’s request. The paper presents MarioGPT as, to the authors’ knowledge, the first text-to-level model, with diversity and prompt-based control as central capabilities.

The authors also combine MarioGPT with novelty search to support open-ended exploration. The resulting levels vary in their player paths, linking diversity to play-style dynamics as well as generated layouts. The contribution brings together language-based steering and a search process for discovering increasingly varied content, offering a way to keep exploration going while retaining a means of expressing generation intentions.
neurips-2023-mariogpt-open-ended-text2le.tldr: MarioGPT generates Mario levels from text prompts and combines with novelty search to discover increasingly diverse layouts and player paths.

paragraphs: Multi-task learning improves related models by using similarities between their tasks. In practice, pooling information can be difficult when organizations cannot share their underlying data, particularly in healthcare. This paper develops a framework that works with summary statistics from different sources, allowing related tasks to inform one another under that access constraint.

The framework also addresses how to choose its tuning parameters when individual records are unavailable. An adaptive procedure based on a variant of Lepski’s method selects parameters from the accessible summaries. This is an important part of making the approach usable: the restricted information must support both fitting the models and deciding how to tune the learning procedure.

The authors provide finite-sample theory covering different source dataset sizes and degrees of overlap, then investigate the theoretical findings through extensive simulations. The results characterize performance across these regimes rather than assuming all sources contribute equally useful information. The work offers a route to training related models with restricted data sharing, with genetic risk prediction identified as a potential application.
neurips-2023-multi-task-learning-with-su.tldr: A multi-task learning framework trains and adaptively tunes related models using only summary statistics from different data sources.

paragraphs: This paper examines whether attackers can steer large vision-language models toward chosen responses by manipulating image inputs. It focuses on black-box access, where an attacker can interact with the target system without accessing its internal parameters. The concern is that vulnerability in the visual input can affect the behavior of the entire multimodal system.

The evaluation first constructs targeted adversarial examples against pretrained models such as CLIP and BLIP. It then transfers those examples to other vision-language systems, including MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, UniDiffuser, BLIP-2, and Img2Prompt. This tests whether manipulations developed using one model can induce a desired response from another model.

The authors further find that queries to the target systems improve attack effectiveness, reporting high success in obtaining targeted responses. The findings provide quantitative evidence of vulnerability in the evaluated open-source models under this access setting. They motivate more thorough security evaluation before deployment, particularly evaluations that consider how image manipulations can redirect generated language rather than only disrupt visual recognition.
neurips-2023-on-evaluating-adversarial-r.tldr: Transferred image attacks, strengthened through black-box queries, induced targeted responses from the evaluated open-source vision-language models.

paragraphs: This paper studies reinforcement learning with safety constraints applied at individual decision steps. Its formulation does not assume that a safe action is always available, reflecting situations where avoiding every violation may be impossible. The goal is to control violations while still learning to obtain reward, rather than relying on a permanently available safe choice.

The proposed SUCBVI algorithm has theoretical bounds on both step-wise violation and regret. Its violation bound scales as the square root of the number of states times the total interaction steps, with logarithmic factors suppressed; the authors also provide a gap-dependent alternative. Lower bounds establish optimal dependence on state count and total steps for both violation and regret.

The paper additionally considers safe exploration before a reward function is supplied. Its SRF-UCRL algorithm seeks a near-optimal safe policy with nearly state-of-the-art sample complexity while controlling violations during exploration. Experiments support the theoretical results and report better safety performance. These guarantees bound violations during learning; they do not assert that every individual action is violation-free.
neurips-2023-provably-safe-reinforcement.tldr: Two reinforcement-learning algorithms bound step-wise safety violations without assuming safe actions always exist.

paragraphs: This paper studies nonconvex optimization when some data points have been arbitrarily corrupted. The target is an approximate second-order stationary point, a solution characterized by both its gradient and curvature. Such points are widely studied with ordinary stochastic data, but adversarial outliers make reliable optimization substantially harder.

The authors propose a general efficient framework under strong contamination, where a constant fraction of data can be corrupted. Its accuracy guarantee does not depend on ambient dimension. Its sample requirement does: it uses roughly D squared divided by epsilon samples, suppressing logarithmic factors, where D is the ambient dimension and epsilon is the corruption fraction.

Applied to low-rank matrix sensing, the framework yields provably robust algorithms that tolerate corruption in both sensing matrices and measurements. A Statistical Query lower bound supplies evidence that quadratic dependence on dimension in the sample requirement is necessary for computationally efficient methods. The distinction matters: dimension-independent accuracy does not imply dimension-independent data requirements, and the lower-bound evidence is tied to a particular computational framework.
neurips-2023-robust-second-order-nonconv.tldr: A robust optimization framework finds approximate second-order stationary points with dimension-independent accuracy despite arbitrary data corruption.

paragraphs: Vision transformers must balance computational cost with preserving detailed image information. Downsampling operations such as pooling reduce computation but can discard information because they are not invertible. Scattering Vision Transformer addresses this tension by treating low-frequency and high-frequency image components separately rather than relying on that form of information reduction.

The architecture includes a spectral scattering network to capture fine image details. It also uses a spectral gating network with Einstein multiplication to mix information across tokens and channels while reducing complexity. These components combine a way to represent image detail with a less costly mechanism for exchanging information within the model.

The authors report state-of-the-art ImageNet performance alongside reductions in parameters and FLOPs. The small, base, and large variants reach 84.2%, 85.2%, and 85.7% top-1 accuracy, respectively. Results are comparable on other vision tasks such as instance segmentation, while transfer-learning evaluations outperform other transformers on the listed datasets. The findings support spectral processing as a useful architectural choice for both efficiency and visual recognition.
neurips-2023-scattering-vision-transform.tldr: Scattering Vision Transformer combines frequency-separated image representations and spectral mixing to improve recognition with fewer parameters and operations.

paragraphs: A world model helps a reinforcement-learning agent represent its environment, but accurate environment modeling does not automatically emphasize what matters for the agent’s task. Models focused on value can offer greater task awareness while sacrificing semantic information and presenting implementation difficulties. TEMPO aims to combine task relevance with the richer representations of maximum-likelihood models.

The framework adds a second optimization level that learns how much weight to assign each training sample. At the upper level, a meta weighter network minimizes a task-aware model loss. At the lower level, the world model learns from the weighted samples, concentrating on important examples while maintaining semantic information in its state representations.

The authors evaluate TEMPO on continuous and discrete control tasks from the DeepMind Control Suite and Atari games. They report state-of-the-art results in eventual performance, training stability, and convergence speed. The contribution is a way to align model training with the task through learned sample importance, while keeping the underlying environment-modeling objective as part of the learning process.
neurips-2023-task-aware-world-model-lear.tldr: TEMPO learns task-aware sample weights through two-level optimization to improve world-model learning and control performance.

paragraphs: This paper uses the covariance of internal representations to study the behavior of very deep and wide attention networks. Covariance acts as a proxy for trainability, describing how representations relate to one another. The analysis considers initialization as depth and width grow together proportionally, rather than increasing one while keeping the other fixed.

To obtain a well-defined limit, the authors modify attention by centering the Softmax output at the identity and introducing a width-dependent temperature for its logits. The limiting covariance distribution follows a stochastic differential equation indexed by the depth-to-width ratio. Residual connections provide control over both its drift and diffusion, the components governing systematic change and random fluctuation.

A stable limiting equation implies well-behaved covariance even at very large scale, preventing the rank degeneracy addressed by the analysis. Simulations also show that the equation describes corresponding finite models surprisingly well. These architectural changes define the shaped Transformer, connecting attention design to a tractable account of representation stability at initialization.
neurips-2023-the-shaped-transformer-atte.tldr: Modified attention and residual connections yield a tractable, stable covariance limit as Transformer depth and width grow together.

paragraphs: Knowledge-based visual question answering combines evidence from an image with knowledge beyond that image. Passing a general caption or object list to a language model can omit a crucial detail or include distracting information. TOA addresses this by making the question and a proposed answer guide which visual evidence the system collects.

The language model first forms an initial hypothesis using its knowledge. It then actively gathers evidence needed to check that hypothesis through vision modules. These modules support spatial attention, deciding where to look, and attribute attention, deciding what to look for. Image understanding therefore becomes a task-oriented process rather than a fixed description prepared independently of the reasoning.

On open-ended knowledge-based visual question answering datasets, the method outperforms the evaluated baselines. The authors also report a clearer reasoning procedure and improved interpretability. The approach matters because it connects a model’s knowledge-based proposal to explicit visual verification, allowing the visual information supplied to the language model to be selected for the particular question being answered.
neurips-2023-toa-task-oriented-active-vq.tldr: TOA forms an answer hypothesis, then actively selects visual evidence to verify it and improve knowledge-based visual question answering.

paragraphs: Generative data augmentation adds labeled examples produced by a model trained on the original dataset. Those examples are not independent of the training data, and their distribution may differ from the true one. This paper develops a stability-based theoretical analysis that accounts for both complications when studying classification performance.

The bound includes the divergence between the generated and true distributions. A faster learning rate is possible when that divergence shrinks sufficiently quickly: its order must be smaller than max(log(m) times beta_m, 1/sqrt(m)), where m is training-set size and beta_m is the stability constant. The result is conditional, so adding generated examples alone does not establish a faster rate.

For the specific Gaussian mixture and generative adversarial network settings analyzed, augmentation does not improve the learning rate. It can nevertheless improve guarantees by a constant amount when training sets are small, where overfitting is particularly consequential. Simulations and empirical evaluations support these conclusions, distinguishing a better guarantee at small sample sizes from a better asymptotic rate.
neurips-2023-toward-understanding-genera.tldr: Generative augmentation can improve learning guarantees, but faster rates require sufficiently small mismatch between generated and true data distributions.

paragraphs: Minimax optimization alternates between variables that minimize an objective and variables that maximize it. Many algorithms depend on structural conditions that are difficult to verify in practice. This paper proposes doubly smoothed gradient descent ascent, or DS-GDA, a single-loop method designed to balance the two sides without choosing a different algorithm for each supported problem class.

With the same hyperparameters, DS-GDA handles nonconvex-concave, convex-nonconcave, and nonconvex-nonconcave problems satisfying the stated one-sided KŁ properties, with complexity O(epsilon^-4). Knowing the KŁ exponent can sharpen the bound to O(epsilon^(-2 max(2 theta, 1))) for theta between zero and one. The authors report that these bounds match the corresponding best existing results.

The paper also demonstrates practical convergence on challenging nonconvex-nonconcave examples beyond the regularity conditions used for the guarantees. DS-GDA escapes limit cycles in all the listed examples, including Forsaken and PolarGame. These demonstrations broaden the empirical case for the method, while the formal complexity guarantees remain attached to their specified structural conditions.
neurips-2023-universal-gradient-descent-.tldr: DS-GDA uses one balanced minimax update scheme across several structured problem classes and escapes cycles in challenging additional examples.
